instance.isolation: Real express + production mountMcpGateway + production bearer middleware on a loopback socket, with a real better-sqlite3 file, real session rows and real transcript JSONL files in a throwaway directory. The control service is scripted to answer the delivery id the transcript carries. No live fleet instance, operator database or operator ~/.quay-fleet stream was read or written; production deployment verification is left to F10.

tools.name: knowledge_facts
tools.description: Read one versioned knowledge-application fact about this host: `peer_result` (the ask a session stated, the settling reply re-read from the transcript, the same operation id on both readings, and — when the query names a `deliveryId` — the cross-session delivery chain the server saved at acceptance: the delivery record, the target transcript row whose id IS that delivery, and the FIRST assistant turn after it; that chain is `verified` only when every link agrees, an answer is never borrowed from before the delivery, and a reply grants no action permission), `effective_config` (expected, stored and actually-running model / effort / permission mode, the operation the reading is about, the ACTUAL request and response the provider recorded for that operation, and a per-field verdict — `verified` is false when the operation, any layer or any expected field is unknown, and a field the provider cannot read back is declared unavailable in `capabilities` rather than echoed from the stored row), or `inventory` (a bounded session page that keeps its filters, total and truncation, so an empty page is never reported as an empty host). Every field is either an evidence reading with its source and observation time, or an explicit `unknown` with a reason; the payload also carries the contract name and version, the build id and the running process boot id.

tools.name: session_send
tools.description: Send a message to a session, returning the run id at once. A queued message does not answer a pending approval; use approval_answer to answer it. An optional opaque correlation label: it is only stored on the run and echoed on the audit record, never interpreted or advanced by the server.
